entries.title: What we know about stabbing on Flydubai flight to Israel
entries.snippet: A pilot has been arrested and is being questioned after another pilot was stabbed, officials say.

entries.title: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine
entries.snippet: A foreign policy speech by the Russian president will be keenly watched, but all signs point to the full-scale invasion continuing.

entries.title: US Supreme Court allows execution of Christa Pike to go ahead
entries.snippet: The death by lethal injection was scheduled to happen earlier on Wednesday before a lower court paused the execution.

entries.title: Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss, threatening water supplies
entries.snippet: Scientists say such rapid melting is no longer surprising given the pace of climate change.

entries.title: Six smugglers jailed for manslaughter over worst Channel small boats disaster
entries.snippet: Thirty-one migrants died when their boat went down in November 2021. The trial found that the guilty men were part of two smuggling networks.

entries.title: Tiny image sparks big backlash in Nikon photo contest
entries.snippet: Dr Ning Xu denies he broke the rules of Nikon's annual Small World In Motion contest.

entries.title: California bans child marriage, a practice still legal in 32 US states
entries.snippet: Gov Gavin Newsom called it a "long overdue measure to protect young Californians".

entries.title: Trekkers helicoptered off mountains as more deadly landslides hit Nepal
entries.snippet: A month after mass catastrophic flooding, around 30 people have died in landslides and heavy rain.

entries.title: Russia launches largest attack on Ukraine energy infrastructure since spring
entries.snippet: In total 11 regions of the country were attacked overnight, with residential buildings and railways also targeted, the Ukrainian PM says.

entries.title: Last UK and US troops leave Iraq as anti-Islamic State mission ends
entries.snippet: The withdrawal of coalition forces, under a deal agreed two years ago, was a key demand of the Iraqi government.

entries.title: Ethiopia fighting escalates in Tigray killing 52 civilians, medic tells the BBC
entries.snippet: The deadly fighting has also spread to neighbouring regions, stranding tourists in Lalibela.

entries.title: Girl has multiple surgeries to control infections after strike in Gaza
entries.snippet: Witnesses say Raseel's tent was hit by an Israeli helicopter strike. Israel’s military says it has no record of the attack.

entries.title: US actor Chad Lowe 'heartbroken' by death of daughter Fiona aged 13
entries.snippet: Lowe and his wife Kim Painter announce the death of their daughter, who "was the light of our lives".

entries.title: Chinese AI tool told researchers how to make bioweapons
entries.snippet: Mindgard said it discovered in July that Kimi models K2.6 and K3 Swarm could evade developer's safety limits.

entries.title: Singapore launches matchmaking service for government workers
entries.snippet: The launch of FirstDate comes as the ageing nation wrestles with a record-low fertility rate.

entries.title: Africa's richest man launches Kenya oil refinery despite land protests
entries.snippet: The Kenya refinery is part of Dangote's ambitious bid to expand and help industralise Africa by 2030.

entries.title: 'He will never walk free': Indian judge's letter promises child sex abuse survivor
entries.snippet: In the emotional letter, the judge describes the survivor as "the bravest little girl this court has ever seen".

entries.title: Botswana condemned for slaughtering 23 elephants for independence celebrations
entries.snippet: The government authorises the hunting of elephants and dozens of other wild animals for independence day feasts.

entries.title: Six Flags shuts down X2 rollercoaster after more than 100 allege brain injuries
entries.snippet: Hundreds of riders were allegedly injured on X2, which has seats that spin 360 degrees.

entries.title: China has cracked down on AI relationships. Is it ahead of the game?
entries.snippet: Beijing has cracked down on AI chatbots that can replicate human relationships. Experts are asking if this is the right thing to do.

entries.title: Swiss glaciers suffer another year of record ice loss
entries.snippet: Switzerland's glaciers are disappearing at a record pace. More than 5% of their ice has vanished this year alone — threatening water supplies, ecosystems and communities across Europe.

entries.title: Leaning into culture war flashpoints, Hegseth says he has transformed U.S. military
entries.snippet: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told hundreds of junior military officers and enlisted leaders on Wednesday that the Trump administration has achieved a cultural shift in the military.

entries.title: Greetings from Syria, where time seems to melt as a glassmaker braves scorching temps
entries.snippet: As a Syrian glassmaker created his wares in Damascus, watching his craft reminded this reporter to slow down and enjoy the moment.

entries.title: Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong
entries.snippet: The Cornell lawsuit filed by a woman alleging a brutal rape raises questions on how police handle such cases. The majority of police lack adequate training on trauma-informed approaches, experts say.

entries.title: Trump officials changed forms for overseas voters amid a GOP push to restrict voting
entries.snippet: The Pentagon made last-minute changes to forms that many overseas U.S. citizens use for absentee voting, removing a category of citizens that Republicans have been pushing to block from voting.

entries.title: How Ukrainians are coping with new, more deadly Russian attacks
entries.snippet: Zanny Minton Beddoes, The Economist's editor in chief , just visited Ukraine. She says, despite all its drone weaponry, Kyiv is under extraordinary bombardment, as Russia tries to make it unlivable.

entries.title: How Trump keeps undercutting his anti-communist message
entries.snippet: The Trump administration has taken government equity stakes in more than three dozen private companies.

entries.title: After failed execution, health workers say Tennessee's method flouts medical ethics
entries.snippet: After a botched lethal injection in May, dozens of Tennessee medical professionals told the governor that healthcare professionals shouldn't help with executions, no matter the method.

entries.title: On flight to Israel, pilot is stabbed, plane plunges before passengers tackle attacker
entries.snippet: As the plane went into a spin and began to plunge, passengers and crew members got into the cockpit, subdued the pilot and diverted the flight to land in Saudi Arabia, Israel's leader says.

entries.title: FBI hunting the hackers who stole its employees' sensitive data
entries.snippet: The FBI says it's addressing a massive data breach, vowing to go after the hackers it believes are responsible.

entries.title: Woman accused of firing at Rihanna's home indicted on attempted murder with assault weapon
entries.snippet: A Florida woman accused of driving across the country to fire a rifle at Rihanna and A$AP Rocky's home, hitting a trailer the celebrity couple was inside and a nursery where their kids were, has been indicted by a grand jury on 14 felony counts including attempted murder.

entries.title: Federal oversight of Oakland Police Department ends after 23 years
entries.snippet: A federal judge on Tuesday ended federal monitoring of the Oakland Police Department after 23 years, capping the longest-running oversight of a police department in U.S. history.

entries.title: Passengers describe stopping pilot's alleged attempt to crash Israel-bound flight

entries.snippet: In 2024, Wall Street Journal correspondent Evan Gershkovich was freed from detention in Russia, as part of a complex prisoner swap that included 16 people from seven countries. Gershkovich sat down with Amna Nawaz to discuss his arrest, his time in prison and his new book, "This

entries.title: Is the American Dream still achievable for younger generations?
entries.snippet: The American Dream. The phrase has been a national ethos for generations. But what does it mean today, and how achievable is it? Judy Woodruff has a look for her series, Crossroads: America at 250.

entries.title: Democrats want a blue wave. New Hampshire is Exhibit A for why that may not happen

entries.title: Tropical Pacific moisture drenches central U.S. as another Pacific hurricane forms
entries.snippet: Tropical weather that surged onshore from the Pacific soaked more of the U.S. on Wednesday while forecasters announced yet another hurricane off the coast of Mexico.

entries.title: Senate reaches bipartisan deal on permitting bill to speed approvals of new energy projects
entries.snippet: Senators from both parties said Wednesday they have reached a bipartisan deal on legislation aimed at speeding up permitting reviews for new energy and infrastructure projects that now face yearslong delays as lawmakers seek to meet growing demand for electricity and other forms

entries.title: WATCH: Justice Department files complaint against judges over immigration enforcement surge comments
entries.snippet: The Department of Justice filed a complaint Wednesday against federal judges in Minnesota over their remarks to the media about the pressure on their courthouse during Trump administration's immigration enforcement surge.

entries.title: WATCH: Trump announces $54 billion South Korean investment in Alaska natural gas pipeline
entries.snippet: The announcement marks the second time this week that the Republican president has sought to highlight the promise of foreign investment made possible by his administration's trade policy in states where Republican Senate candidates are in tight election campaigns.

entries.title: What to know about the terrifying FlyDubai flight forced to land in Saudi Arabia
entries.snippet: One pilot stabbed another and attempted to crash a flight from the United Arab Emirates to Israel, according to Israel's prime minister. Here's what we know — and don't know — about what happened on FlyDubai flight FZ1073.

entries.title: WATCH: Data center bill falls short as Senate holds final votes before the midterms
entries.snippet: A bill that attempts to address voter worries about data centers and their impact on energy costs failed to advance in the Senate on Wednesday, falling victim to an election-year clash on how best to address a growing concern.

entries.title: Former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem files for divorce from her husband of 34 years
entries.snippet: Former Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem has filed for divorce from her husband of 34 years.

entries.title: WATCH: Hegseth confirms the U.S. military will cut 20% of its generals and admirals
entries.snippet: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed Wednesday that the U.S. military will cut 20% of its generals and admirals as he delivered what he is calling his "State of the Force" address.

entries.title: No criminal wrongdoing in Federal Reserve building renovation, watchdog says, but it was mismanaged
entries.snippet: The Federal Reserve's internal watchdog said Wednesday that the agency has broadly mismanaged an expansive building renovation project but did not find any criminal violations, as alleged by Trump administration prosecutors.

entries.title: Court halts execution of Christa Gail Pike for a Tennessee murder she committed at age 18

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Gaza: NGO reports dire camp conditions, says Israel is moving 'Yellow Line'
entries.snippet: The Danish Refugee Council alleges that Israel is employing "a policy of protracted displacement" in Gaza. It says the so-called "Yellow Line" is creeping west toward the coast, preventing many from returning home.

entries.title: Five EU states plan first deportation center in Africa for 2027
entries.snippet: Greece, Germany, Austria, Denmark and the Netherlands are moving forward with plans to establish deportation centers outside the EU. An African partner country has reportedly already been selected.

entries.title: Flydubai pilot investigated over possible attempt to crash Tel Aviv-bound flight
entries.snippet: A Flydubai service from the UAE to Israel made an emergency landing after the copilot stabbed the captain. Eyewitnesses said he attempted to crash the plane before he was subdued by passengers.

entries.title: France's Macron, Spain's Sanchez welcome idea of UK rejoining EU after Burnham remarks
entries.snippet: During a visit to Spain, France's Emmanuel Macron said it would be "good news" if the UK moves towards the EU, with Pedro Sanchez also embracing the idea. UK PM Andy Burnham has not ruled out rejoining the bloc.

entries.title: Are the Houthis winning against Saudi Arabia?
entries.snippet: It's unclear how the Saudis can defuse the threat presented by the Houthis in next-door Yemen or who they can turn to for help. The US isn't interested, the Europeans are hedging and nobody wants open conflict with Iran.

entries.title: Germany debates alleged antisemitism in the Left Party
entries.snippet: The Central Council of Jews in Germany thinks the Left Party is dangerous. Other Jews, however, are showing solidarity with the party. How does that add up?

entries.title: Senegal's Youth Olympics makes Olympics in Africa 'logical'
entries.snippet: The Youth Olympics are to be hosted in Africa for the first time ever. The edition in Senegal is also a chance to prove the continent can host a full Olympics in the future.

entries.title: African leaders herald $16B Dangote oil refinery in Kenya
entries.snippet: An oil refinery on Kenya's coast is expected to be completed in 40 months, and will process an estimated 700,000 barrels of oil per day. Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, will lead the project.

entries.title: Germany raises Deutschlandticket price to €66.80 a month from 2027 under new cost-based formula
entries.snippet: A new cost-based formula has pushed up the price of Germany's nationwide public transport pass for 2027.

entries.title: Iran's nuclear program remains shrouded in mystery as the regime debates ditching non-proliferation
entries.snippet: Iran's nuclear program is entering a critical phase as Tehran debates dropping out of a nuclear non-proliferation treaty. Satellite images also show activity at known nuclear sites.

entries.title: Lawyer of Junaid Hafeez, a Pakistai scholar imprisoned for 13 years, is hopeful for his release
entries.snippet: A former Fullbright scholar, Junaid Hafeez was sentenced to death under Pakistan's controversial blasphemy laws. His family and lawyer told DW there is now hope a court will overturn the conviction.

entries.title: Manchester City Premier League charges: What do they mean?
entries.snippet: Since being bought by the UAE in 2008, Manchester City have become one of the world's most successful football clubs. A raft of serious financial charges threatens to undermine this and bring chaos to the Premier League.

entries.title: Servers at Munich's iconic Oktoberfest call for more respect
entries.snippet: Oktoberfest is famous the world over for beer, brass band music and Bavarian traditions. But staff at the Wiesn are also reporting incidents of racism and sexism. They're taking a stand against discrimination.

entries.title: Bosnia elections: Polls overshadowed by exhaustion, exodus and geopolitics as ethnic politics eclipse real problems
entries.snippet: Bosnia goes to the polls on October 4 to elect several parliaments and presidents. While voters worry about the economy and emigration, the campaign is focused on ethnicity, exposing the country's political paralysis.

entries.title: Is US President Donald Trump right to rename AI as 'Super Intelligence'?
entries.snippet: Donald Trump thinks the name artificial intelligence sounds "fake" and has ordered US agencies to use "Super Intelligence" instead. Yet, tech firms and researchers have little reason to play along.

entries.title: Ireland will boycott Eurovision again because of Israel's participation, but the song contest is still expanding.
entries.snippet: The 2026 Eurovision Song Contest was marred by boycotts in protest against Israel's participation in the midst of its war on Gaza. It still aims to keep growing.

entries.title: South Korea: Lost shark draws over half a million visitors
entries.snippet: The South Korean port of Busan says that a stranded shark has become a major tourist draw. It's also named the ocean predator an honorary ambassador to the city.

entries.title: Eiffel Tower chief Patrick Branco Ruivo to step down after female staff excluded during Hindu group's visit
entries.snippet: An investigation found management failures led to female Eiffel Tower staff being excluded during a Hindu group's visit.

entries.title: India news: Key opposition leaders meet to discuss poll body row
entries.snippet: India's opposition leaders meet in New Delhi to push back against voter roll revisions and discuss poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar. DW has more.
